body.heading: Ready is a moving target
paragraphs: Waiting to feel ready sounds sensible, but the feeling rarely arrives on schedule. Skills grow by doing the thing badly at first, and confidence tends to follow action rather than precede it.
Think of the last thing you learned. You were almost certainly unready on day one, and it worked out anyway, one awkward attempt at a time.

body.heading: Make the start embarrassingly small
paragraphs: Choose a first step so small it feels slightly silly: open the document, lay out the tools, play one scale, write one sentence. Small steps bypass the negotiation that big plans trigger.
Once you have started, continuing is a different and easier decision. If you stop after the tiny step, you still started, and starting again tomorrow is easier than starting from zero.

takeaway: Do not wait to feel ready; start small and let readiness catch up.
